language_wrapper: Consider the cubic polynomial P(k) = {a3}k^3 + {a2}k^2 + {a1}k + {a0}. Define S = sum over k = {l} to [u] of (P(k+4) - P(k)) * cos((pi/2) * k * (k - 1)). Compute the exact value of |S|.
hardness_rationale: The seed relies on recognizing that cos((pi/2) * k(k-1)) yields a simple 4-periodic sign on triangular numbers, allowing grouping or parity analysis. This family upgrades the task by inserting a step-4 finite difference (P(k+4) - P(k)) of a cubic polynomial under the same root-of-unity filter. The key advanced idea is to exploit the exact period-4 invariance of the sign to telescope the entire long sum down to only eight boundary terms, which requires recognizing the period-aligned finite-difference trick (Delta_4) rather than straightforward parity grouping. Handling a general cubic P and a broad index range forces careful boundary accounting and prevents trivial guessing, substantially increasing the algebraic and conceptual difficulty while preserving the core periodic-sign logic of the original.
notes: Solution outline: Let s(k) = cos((pi/2) * k(k-1)) in {+1, -1}. Since s(k+4) = s(k), set F(k) = s(k) * P(k). Then sum_{k=l}^u s(k)[P(k+4) - P(k)] = sum_{k=l}^u [F(k+4) - F(k)] = sum_{j=u+1}^{u+4} F(j) - sum_{j=l}^{l+3} F(j). The absolute value of this integer is the final answer.
